doc.title: Phoebe Jacobs and Jackie Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006

title: Armstrong music therapy program at Beth Israel
summary: Jacobs explains how Louis sent music to his nephew Clarence, leading to the Armstrong Music Therapy Program.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: That’s for sure. You’re right. Well we know that because we have music therapy in the hospital named for Louis and we know what it’s done. Because Louis had a nephew who had a problem and he put him in a mental institution after nobody in the family could take care of him anymore. And the boy was, well he was a man of 32 and he was not acting properly and when Louis came to visit him he knew one thing, that Clarence didn’t have any music where he was, where he had always been in an atmosphere of music. So he insisted that this facility at least allow him to send some music that Clarence could enjoy because it wasn’t only Louis’ music that he sent. He sent classical music as well and religious music. And the institution felt that this was wonderful for their patients. So consequently when he died Beth Israel Hospital was a hospital that he loved very much and was a patient at, we succeeded in having them do the Louis and Lucille Armstrong Music Therapy Program which is in existence for twelve years, and it’s been expanding and is now going to take care of musicians as well as people that just happen to be hospitalized. © Fillius Jazz Archive -20-
